Also recommending kdenlive. It's a really easy to use and fairly powerful video editor and I've put together a few videos using it with no problem. Nothing is going to be as absolutely powerful as the best editors for Windows and Mac but I think kdenlive is more than good enough for most people.

I Highly recommend learning the ffmpeg command interface, time and time again I have tried to use GUI applications for simple stuff but I always end up going back to the cmd line because of its simplicity and stability.

That being said:

  • kdenlive is the application I would 'goto' if it wasn't so tied to kde now. I've used it in the past and it does work very nicely
  • Lightworks is very good, I've been playing with it more and more, if all you want is 720p video for youtube then it is now the front runner IMHO
  • blender is way too cumbersome for video editing, the workflow is designed around 3d compositing so a lot of the interface gets in the way. there are add-ons that help a little but IMHO its just not clean enough. An interface mod for blender that took all the extra shit away for simple video editing would probably gain a lot of traction.
  • openshot I'm still waiting for a release of the new version, the one that is available now is ok for really simple stuff.
  • shotcut was too unstable last time i looked at it. hopefully its improved, i like the look of it.

I do most of my work on clips split from source video using ffmpeg, de-shaked using ffmpeg, composited with natron(transform and colour correct), slowmovideo for retiming, then probably blender or lightworks for assembly and transitions, might even be worth purchasing a licence for lightworks if i needed to export 1080p

The editing application you use doesn't really form the bulk of the difficulty of video editing IMHO, understanding formats, codecs, regions, optimal use case, shooting the source material itself etc.
